skill.name: hig-technologies
skill.description: Apple HIG reference skill for technology integrations. Covers Siri, Apple Pay, HealthKit, HomeKit, ARKit, iCloud, Sign in with Apple, CarPlay, and related features.
skill.summary: Guides Apple technology integrations with HIG checklists for privacy, permissions, flows, and testing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 170 static findings against the skill context. They are false positives from HIG prose, Markdown links, image alt text, and inline code formatting. No executable code, shell command invocation, automatic network access, environment access, or prompt injection was found.

content.value_statement: Apple technology integrations can fail review when privacy, permissions, or platform patterns are unclear. This skill turns Apple HIG guidance into practical checklists for supported frameworks.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes Apple HIG guidance for Siri, Apple Pay, HealthKit, HomeKit, ARKit, iCloud, Wallet, Maps, and related technologies.
Produces implementation checklists with required features, optional features, privacy notes, and testing guidance.
Identifies user flows for permissions, authentication, payments, shared experiences, and accessibility.
Cross-references related HIG skills for inputs, system components, and status indicators.
Highlights user-facing risks for sensitive domains such as health, identity, payments, smart home, and driving.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not API implementation code.
It does not replace current App Store Review Guidelines or entitlement approval.
It cannot verify whether Apple documentation changed after the included references were authored.
It depends on user-provided product context for precise recommendations.

use_cases.title: Plan an Apple Pay checkout
use_cases.description: Map purchase details, payment button placement, authorization states, receipts, and fallback payment paths before engineering starts.

use_cases.title: Review HealthKit permission flows
use_cases.description: Check whether health data requests explain value, ask only for needed access, and provide understandable recovery paths.

use_cases.title: Adapt iPad features to Mac Catalyst
use_cases.description: Use Mac-specific guidance for menus, keyboard behavior, pointer support, windowing, and platform expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a technology checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one Apple framework or service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation checklist for [Apple technology] in a [platform] app. Include required behavior, optional enhancements, privacy needs, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Compare permission approaches
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of two design options.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two permission flows for [feature]. Explain which better follows Apple HIG guidance for [technology] and why.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a user journey
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced evaluation of an existing product flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this [technology] user journey against Apple HIG guidance: [paste flow]. Identify risks, missing states, and review-ready fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-technology launch plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across several Apple platform features.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a launch plan for an app using [technology A], [technology B], and [technology C]. Cover user value, consent, edge cases, accessibility, and testing.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to add Sign in with Apple to an existing account system.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering standard button placement, account linking, hidden email handling, fallback states, and testing.

output_examples.input: A designer wants to validate an AR room scanning flow.
output_examples.output: A review of setup guidance, lighting prompts, surface detection states, exit paths, non-AR alternatives, and privacy messaging.

output_examples.input: A product manager needs Tap to Pay guidance for merchants.
output_examples.output: A concise flow covering merchant activation, payment authorization progress, failed tap recovery, result screens, and receipt options.

best_practices: Start with the specific Apple technology, target platforms, user goal, and data permissions.
Ask for privacy, accessibility, and error states in the same prompt as the main flow.
Use the output as design guidance, then verify API details in current Apple developer documentation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for generic Apple design advice without naming the technology or user task.
Do not treat the skill as legal, medical, payment compliance, or App Store approval advice.
Do not copy guidance into UI text without adapting it to your product and locale.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides Apple HIG design guidance, implementation checklists, permission notes, and testing considerations.

faq.question: Which Apple technologies are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Siri, Apple Pay, HealthKit, HomeKit, ARKit, iCloud, Wallet, Maps, CarPlay, Game Center, and related features.

faq.question: Can it help with privacy-sensitive features?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights user consent, data minimization, permission timing, and clear explanations for sensitive Apple technologies.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it to structure design work, then verify API details and review rules with current Apple sources.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I get the best output?
faq.answer: Provide the Apple technology, platform, user goal, permission needs, and any existing flow details.
